workflows.name: Order to shipment
workflows.trigger: A customer places an order that needs to be shipped
steps: Create order with line items
Select or confirm shipping address
Convert order to one or more shipments
Pack parcels per shipment
Continue into the shipment lifecycle

provenance.notes: Steps and entities from karrio's orders module (Order.DIRECT_PROPS, Shipment.order_id) and fleetbase_orders; state names are verbatim from karrio's OrderStatus enum (unfulfilled/partial/fulfilled/delivered/cancelled).

workflows.name: Shipment lifecycle
workflows.trigger: A shipment is booked with a carrier after rate selection
steps: Request rates from connected carriers
Select a rate and purchase label
Hand off to carrier (pickup or drop-off)
Carrier scans update transit status
Out for delivery
Delivered, or exception raised

provenance.notes: State names and the linear progression are verbatim from karrio's ShipmentStatus enum (single source for exact values); the general multi-stage creation-to-delivery shape is cross-referenced against fleetbase's order lifecycle flags (dispatched/started/status), which is why this is scored medium rather than low.

workflows.name: Tracking and visibility
workflows.trigger: A carrier or driver scan/webhook event arrives for a shipment
steps: Receive carrier webhook or telematics event
Normalize to a tracking event with status/code/location
Append to the shipment's tracking timeline
Push update to customer-facing tracking page
Notify customer on major status change

provenance.notes: State vocabulary is verbatim from karrio's TrackerStatus enum and cross-referenced against fleetbase's fleetbase_tracking_statuses table (same states list already used for the tracking_event entity). A state_machine is included as a best-effort progression; in practice carrier scans can arrive out of order or be re-sent, so implementations should treat transitions as advisory (idempotent on repeated/out-of-order events) rather than strictly enforced, consistent with GS1 EPCIS's event-capture model (std:gs1-epcis) where events are appended to a timeline rather than replacing a single current-state field.

workflows.name: Dispatch and route planning
workflows.trigger: One or more orders are ready to be routed and dispatched
steps: Batch pending orders/stops
Optimize stop sequence into a route
Assign a driver and vehicle
Dispatch the route/manifest to the driver app
Driver executes stops in sequence
Route/manifest marked complete

provenance.notes: Inferred from fleetbase_orders' dispatched/dispatched_at/started/started_at boolean+timestamp pairs; exact status string values are not enumerated in the schema, so state names are reasoned by convention. Single source.

workflows.name: Pickup scheduling
workflows.trigger: A shipper needs a carrier or driver to collect one or more shipments
steps: Choose a pickup date and time window
Schedule pickup with carrier or dispatch
Carrier/driver confirms or the pickup is closed out
Pickup can be cancelled before collection

provenance.notes: Verbatim from karrio's PickupStatus enum; single source.

workflows.name: Proof of delivery capture
workflows.trigger: A driver arrives at the final stop for a delivery
steps: Arrive at delivery stop
Capture signature and/or photo per required pod_method
Upload capture (queued if offline)
Attach to the shipment/order record
Mark stop and order complete

provenance.notes: karrio's delivery_image_url/signature_image_url fields and fleetbase's payloads.pod_method/pod_required columns corroborate that a capture is required and stored, but neither source enumerates a multi-state field for it. The pending_capture/captured/queued_offline/uploaded/attached states and their event names are reasoned from the offline-tolerant mobile capture behaviour described in the domain brief and driver_app feature, not verbatim from either schema; kept at low confidence and flagged here rather than upgraded without a second corroborating source.

workflows.name: Exception and returns handling
workflows.trigger: A delivery attempt fails, damage is reported, or a customer requests a return
steps: Log the exception with type/category/priority
Investigate (contact driver, carrier, or customer)
Decide resolution: redeliver, return, refund, or claim
If returning, generate a return shipment/label
Resolve and close the exception

provenance.notes: fleetbase_issues (type/category/priority/resolved_at) is the direct implementation for the exception lifecycle; karrio's needs_attention/delivery_failed status and return_shipment/is_return fields corroborate the trigger and return path from a second source. The specific open/investigating/resolved/closed state names are reasoned, not verbatim from either schema.

workflows.name: Fleet maintenance scheduling
workflows.trigger: A vehicle approaches a maintenance interval (date, distance, or engine hours)
steps: System computes next_due_date/odometer/engine_hours from the interval
Reminder sent at configured offsets before due
Vehicle is taken out of dispatch rotation for service
Service is recorded, resetting the interval baseline

provenance.notes: fleetbase_maintenance_schedules (interval_method/type/value, next_due_date, reminder_offsets) and traccar's Maintenance model (name/type/start/period), read via `gh api` without cloning, are independent implementations of interval-based scheduling. States match the maintenance_record entity's existing states list; event names (interval_reached, vehicle_taken_out_of_rotation, service_recorded) are reasoned, not verbatim from either schema. A completed record's interval resets by creating a new maintenance_record instance rather than a self-transition.

workflows.name: Warehouse fulfillment
workflows.trigger: Inbound goods arrive at a warehouse, or an order is ready to be picked for outbound shipment
steps: Receive inbound goods against an expected shipment or order
Put away / store received parcels at a location within the facility
Pick parcels for an outbound order
Pack picked items into a shippable parcel
Stage the packed parcel for outbound handoff
Hand off to a carrier or driver (enters the shipment lifecycle)

provenance.notes: Steps and state names are the CBV (Core Business Vocabulary) business-step vocabulary verbatim from GS1 EPCIS 2.0 (verified on disk: JSON-LD-Context/cbv-context-bizstep.jsonld) - receiving, storing, picking, packing, staging_outbound, shipping are all real CBV bizStep values. Kept at medium rather than high because neither cloned implementation (karrio, fleetbase) models an internal warehouse pick/pack/putaway flow; this is standards-only corroboration for a process that is a common capability in warehouse-based logistics operations, not a claim that either source implements it.

workflows.name: Carrier manifest close-out
workflows.trigger: One or more labeled shipments reach the carrier's daily pickup or drop-off cutoff
steps: Generate labels for shipments ready to ship
Group shipments into a carrier close-out manifest
Attach customs documentation for any international shipments in the batch
Submit/close the manifest to the carrier
Carrier confirms receipt of the manifested shipments

provenance.notes: karrio's carrier close-out Manifest model is the direct implementation. GS1's SSCC/GS1-128 standard is the authoritative identifier standard for exactly this kind of grouped 'logistic unit' hand-off. States reuse the manifest entity's existing (reasoned, fleetbase-derived) states list for consistency rather than inventing a second vocabulary.

workflows.name: Customer onboarding and rate setup
workflows.trigger: A new business or individual signs up to ship through the platform
steps: Create the customer/shipper account
Verify identity and billing details
Save and validate shipping addresses
Attach negotiated/contract carrier rates, if any, or fall back to published rates
Account is ready to book shipments

provenance.notes: karrio's OwnedEntity/Address models and fleetbase's company/service-rate schema are the underlying evidence for the individual pieces, but no single source models this as one onboarding process end-to-end; the sequencing is reasoned.

workflows.name: Customs export declaration
workflows.trigger: A shipment crosses an international border and requires a customs declaration
steps: Classify commodities with HS (Harmonized System) codes
Declare value, currency, and content type per commodity
Select the applicable Incoterm to establish who is responsible for duties/customs at each stage
Submit the declaration data alongside the shipment/label purchase
Customs clears the shipment, or holds it for review
Attach the resulting clearance status to the shipment record

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.customs embedded field is the direct implementation. The WCO Data Model is the authoritative harmonized data model for customs (goods) declarations, and Incoterms 2020 standardizes the responsibility-transfer step; however, the specific draft/submitted/cleared/held/rejected state names are reasoned, typical customs terminology, not a literal state enum published by either standard, so this is kept at medium rather than high. Citing these standards is not a claim that any implementation is customs-compliant.

workflows.name: Vehicle telemetry, geofencing, and driver scoring
workflows.trigger: A vehicle's onboard device or telematics provider reports a new GPS/telemetry event
steps: Ingest a telemetry event (position, odometer, engine hours, fuel level)
Update the vehicle's live location and status
Evaluate the position against configured geofences/zones for entry or exit
Aggregate fuel consumption and driving-behavior signals over time
Raise an alert on a geofence violation or fuel anomaly
Roll aggregated signals into a driver performance scorecard

provenance.notes: fleetbase's zones/geofence-state/fuel tables and traccar's Device/Position/Geofence models (read via `gh api` without cloning) corroborate the individual telemetry and geofencing pieces; driver scoring itself is reasoned from fleetbase_issues' driver linkage, not modeled explicitly by either source as a telemetry-derived scorecard, so this combined workflow is kept at low confidence overall.

workflows.name: Load planning and ETA
workflows.trigger: Parcels or orders are ready to be consolidated onto a vehicle for a route
steps: Check vehicle payload/volume capacity against pending parcel or order volume
Consolidate compatible items onto a single vehicle load
Compute an initial ETA per stop from route distance/time
Recompute ETA live from current position and route progress
Alert the customer or dispatcher on a significant delay

provenance.notes: Reasoned from fleetbase_vehicles.payload_capacity and fleetbase_routes/waypoints' total_distance/total_time and time-window fields; no dedicated load-planning or ETA/ML code was inspected in either cloned source, and no second independent source was found. Single source, low confidence, stated here rather than upgraded without evidence.

workflows.name: Freight settlement and claims
workflows.trigger: A shipment is delivered, a carrier invoice arrives, or COD was collected
steps: Receive the carrier invoice or the driver's recorded COD collection
Match invoice line items against the quoted or contracted rate
Flag billing discrepancies for review
Reconcile COD amount collected against the expected amount
File a carrier claim if damage or loss is discovered
Close out the settlement

provenance.notes: karrio's Shipment.applied_fees and fleetbase's payloads.cod_amount/fleetbase_issues tables are independent implementations of the individual pieces. ASC X12 210 (Motor Carrier Freight Details and Invoice) is the standard EDI document for the invoice-matching step specifically, corroborated across multiple independent EDI service-provider descriptions (official X12.org text not accessed). Claims filing itself remains a reasoned extension of fleetbase_issues; no dedicated claims table was found in either source.
